name: ProtectedViewWindow
remarks: A Protected View window is used to display a workbook from a potentially unsafe location. Unsafe locations are defined as the following: - Files opened from the Internet. - Attachments opened from Outlook. - Files blocked by File Block Policy. - Files that fail Office file validation. - Files explicitly opened in Protected View by using the Open in Protected View command of the Open button in the Open dialog box. Workbooks displayed in a Protected View window cannot be edited and are restricted from running active content such as Visual Basic for Applications macros and data connections. For more information about Protected View windows, see What is Protected View? To return a single ProtectedViewWindow object from the ProtectedViewWindows collection, use ProtectedViewWindows (_index_), where _index_ is the index number of the window that you want to open. You can also access the ProtectedViewWindow object that represents the active Protected View window by using the ActiveProtectedViewWindow property of the Application object.
example:
Dim wbProtected As Workbook

If Application.ProtectedViewWindows.Count > 0 Then
    Set wbProtected = Application.ProtectedViewWindows(1).Workbook
End If

properties.name: Caption
properties.description: Returns or sets a Variant value that represents the name that appears in the title bar of the Protected View window. Read/write.

properties.name: EnableResize
properties.description: True if the Protected View window can be resized. Read/write.

properties.name: Height
properties.description: Returns or sets a value that represents the height, in points, of the Protected View window. Read/write.

properties.name: Left
properties.description: Returns or sets a value that represents the distance, in points, from the left edge of the client area to the left edge of the Protected View window. Read/write.

properties.name: Top
properties.description: Returns or sets a value that represents the distance, in points, from the top edge of the specified Protected View window to the top edge of the usable area. Read/write.

properties.name: Width
properties.description: Returns or sets a value that specifies the width, in points, of the specified Protected View window. Read/write.

properties.name: Visible
properties.description: Returns or sets a value that determines whether the specified Protected View window is visible. Read/write.

properties.name: SourceName
properties.description: Returns the name of the source file that is open in the specified Protected View window. Read-only.

properties.name: SourcePath
properties.description: Returns the path of the source file that is open in the specified Protected View window. Read-only.

properties.name: WindowState
properties.description: Returns or sets the state of the specified Protected View window. Read/write.

properties.name: Workbook
properties.description: Returns an object that represents the workbook that is open in the specified Protected View window. Read-only.

methods.name: Activate
methods.description: Brings the Protected View window to the front of the z-order.

methods.name: Close
methods.description: Closes the specified Protected View window.

methods.name: Edit
methods.signature: Edit([WriteResPassword As Variant], [UpdateLinks As Variant]) As Workbook
methods.description: Opens the workbook that is open for editing in the specified Protected View window.

parameters.name: WriteResPassword
parameters.description: The password required to write to a write-reserved workbook. If this argument is omitted and the workbook requires a password, the user will be prompted for the password.

parameters.name: UpdateLinks
parameters.description: Specifies the way that external references (links) in the file, such as the reference to a range in the Budget.xls workbook in the following formula =SUM([Budget.xls]Annual!C10:C25), are updated. If this argument is omitted, the user is prompted to specify how links will be updated. For more information about the values used by this parameter, see the Remarks section. If Excel is opening a file in the WKS, WK1, or WK3 format and the _UpdateLinks_ argument is 0, no charts are created; otherwise, Excel generates charts from the graphs attached to the file.
